findings.claim: User-controlled `depth` and `citation_style` from the REST/MCP entry points are embedded unquoted into a shell command line that the harness is instructed to execute, giving a caller shell-injection into a bypassPermissions session.
findings.evidence: build_prompt constructs the driver line as `--depth {} --citation-style {}` (no shell_quote, unlike query/output_root), and canonical_depth/canonical_citation_style explicitly pass unknown values through unchanged ('an unknown value is passed through unchanged so the driver refuses it visibly' — also restated in references/headless-execution.md 'Value normalisation'). Nothing in the packet shows REST/MCP validating these fields, so `POST /api/v1/jobs` with depth `deep; <arbitrary command>` lands verbatim in a `bash ...` line the harness (claude -p --permission-mode bypassPermissions, or the test fixture's `eval "$CMD"`) is told to run.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject non-canonical depth/citation_style at the daemon (or entry point) with a blocked job and a clear reason instead of passing them through, and shell_quote every interpolated value in the driver line.

findings.claim: After spawning the daemon, spawn_job unconditionally rewrites the checkpoint with `status = "running"`, racing the daemon child and resurrecting jobs that already reached a terminal state into a permanently stuck `running` status.
findings.evidence: New hunk: `let mut updated = checkpoint::read(&job_id)?; match child { Ok(c) => { updated.pid = Some(c.id()); updated.status = "running".to_string(); } ... } checkpoint::write(&updated)?;`. The daemon child starts executing as soon as spawn() returns; its no-harness path (finish_blocked, exercised by the empty-PATH test) or its initial `cp.status = "running"; cp.harness = ...; save()` can complete before the parent's read/write. If the daemon wrote `blocked` and exited, the parent's write overwrites it with `running` and nothing remains to update the job again — the outcome recorded per the spec ('Absence is blocked, not a crash') is silently lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Only transition `pending` -> `running` (compare-and-set on read status), or write the pid into the checkpoint before/atomically with the spawn, and never overwrite a status the daemon has already advanced.

findings.claim: The cancel path is a check-then-act race: `mirror` can overwrite a `cancelled` status written by research_cancel/DELETE between the poll-loop check and mirror's checkpoint write, silently dropping the cancellation.
findings.evidence: The loop reads `checkpoint::read(job_id)` and checks `current.status == "cancelled"` before calling mirror; mirror then performs up to N sequential `sink.status(cp).await` HTTP POSTs (one per newly completed stage) before `save(cp)?` rewrites the whole checkpoint with `cp.status = "running"`. A cancel landing during that window is clobbered, the next poll reads `running`, and the job continues to harness exit, after which the final-state mapping overwrites `cancelled` with complete/blocked/failed. There is no locking or compare-and-swap on the checkpoint file.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-read the checkpoint immediately before every write and abort/merge if the on-disk status is `cancelled`, or guard checkpoint writes with a lock/compare-and-swap so the daemon never overwrites a status it did not write.

findings.claim: The new POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/events ingest endpoint accepts and broadcasts arbitrary AG-UI events with no authentication or validation beyond the job_id match, so any local process can inject forged agent.status/agent.error events into any job's SSE stream and surface bridge.
findings.evidence: ingest_handler deserializes `Json<AguiEvent>`, checks only `event_job_id(&event) != job_id`, then `state.broadcast.send(...)` and forwards to the surface bridge. The doc comment describes it as a trusted channel for the daemon but the packet shows no shared secret, token, or payload sanity check; the daemon's RESEARCH_EVENT_SINK is just a URL.
findings.suggested_fix: Require a shared token (e.g. an env-provided secret header) on ingest, or at minimum validate event shape against the job's known state before broadcasting.

findings.claim: find_package_dir trusts any directory under the shared output root whose checkpoint.json merely contains `stages_planned` or `package_id` plus a matching job_id, so a stale or foreign package written by an earlier run with the same job_id (or a crafted file) is adopted as this job's package and exported.
findings.evidence: `let is_package = v.get("stages_planned").is_some() || v.get("package_id").is_some(); if is_package && v.get("job_id").and_then(|j| j.as_str()) == Some(job_id) { return Some(dir); }` — RESEARCH_OUTPUT_DIR is shared across runs and nothing scopes the search to packages created after this job started (no started_at/mtime comparison), and package_dir then flows into research_export's validate_package.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the package checkpoint's recorded job start time (or the package dir mtime) to be at or after the job's started_at, or have the driver record a per-run nonce the daemon generates and passes via the environment.
